_note: Demo limits for adults on Earth, not medical advice. Each source says which number comes from a source and which is our choice (checked 2026-11-15, docs/sources.md). null = this side never turns red (only yellow).

heart_rate.source: Yellow 100: top of the usual adult resting range (60-100 bpm, commonly cited e.g. AHA; the AHA page was not reachable when checked, 2026-11-15). Yellow low 55: fit people often rest below 60. Red 45/120: our demo choice, not from a source.

bp_sys.source: Yellow 130: start of stage 1 hypertension, AHA/ACC 2025 guideline (categories unchanged since 2017: stage 2 from 140, severe above 180; page not opened, numbers from search summaries, check before the final). Red 160: our choice between stage 2 and severe. Low side (85/95): our demo choice, no source.

bp_dia.source: AHA/ACC 2025: stage 1 from 80, stage 2 from 90, severe above 120 mmHg. Yellow 85 and red 100 are our choice inside stage 1 and stage 2. Low side (50/60): our demo choice, no source.

glucose.source: fasting, mg/dL. High side: NHANES 2021-2023 adults 20-60 without diabetes, 95th/99th percentile (data/processed/nhanes_reference.csv). Low side: Inspiration4 lab reference minimum (OSD-575). No red low until a source is found.

temp.source: CDC: fever is 38.0 °C (100.4 °F) or more (CDC, definitions for ill travelers). Yellow 37.5 is our early sign below fever; red 38.5 is our choice above the fever line, so one borderline reading does not call the ground. Low side 35.0/36.0: our demo choice (35.0 is the usual clinical hypothermia line, source not opened).

sleep_hours.source: Adults need 7 hours or more (AASM/SRS consensus 2015; not opened here, the page asked for a browser check). Yellow under 6 and red under 4 are our choice below that. NASA: in flight crews sleep about 0.3 h a day less than on the ground (OCHMO-TB-041 Sleep Accommodations).

mood.source: Our choice: 1-5 self-report (same scale as PMData); 2 or lower is yellow. No red: mood alone never calls the ground.

exercise_min.source: ISS crews exercise on average 600 min a week (about 85 min a day), aerobic and resistance (OCHMO-TB-031 Exercise Overview, citing Scott et al. 2023). Yellow under 60 min a day is our choice below that; no red.

hrv_ms.source: No population limit: HRV differs a lot between healthy people (LifeSnaps medians 19-100 ms), so only the personal norm is used.

reaction_ms.source: 3-minute PVT: a response slower than 355 ms counts as a lapse (Basner & Rubinstein 2011). Used only before a personal norm exists.
